additional_info.subject: eActros600 - Charging Issues on TER Transports Site – Log Request
additional_info.body:
Dear Teams,
A new Daimler Trucks eActros 600 truck has recently arrived at our TER Transports site, and we are experiencing charging issues with the SIEMENS fast chargers.
We would like to retrieve the charging logs to analyze them and share the findings with Daimler Trucks.
The two affected tractors are:
•     SID: MP / R8 170002535
•     SID: MP / R8 170002536
This morning, a Mercedes eActros600 was connected to Charger 1 – CCS2 connector:
•     The truck was plugged in at 48% SoC
•     Charging was interrupted at 65% SoC, with no clear reason.
Please find attached the summary table of today’s charging tests (17/07) carried out with both Volvo and Mercedes tractors on our SIEMENS fast chargers.
Summary of observations:
•     Significant and erratic fluctuations in charging power (e.g., sudden power drops with no clear pattern)
•     Power delivery appears to be impacted by the presence of another vehicle on the same charger, with no consistent or balanced distribution.
•     Multiple charge interruptions and unusual behavior observed: red warning lights, frozen power levels, abnormal fan noise, etc.
•     The measured values don’t always correlate with the vehicle’s SoC or the rated capabilities of the chargers.
These inconsistencies make it difficult to assess either the performance or the reliability of the chargers or vehicles involved.
I remain available for any further discussion or cross-analysis to help identify the root causes and improve upcoming test sessions.
Thank you in advance.

additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Malek,
I am reaching out from the Expert Services Team in regards of ticket
ID0438853.
The ticket was opened for logs clarifications after a test performed on 17.07.2025 with eActross and Volvo trucks on chargers
tdA3ac
and
AP1DUJ.
Unfortunately, I received the ticket in my hands only this morning, and the logs from EcoG are not available for the sessions from 17.07. As you know, our SECCs have a limited storage memory, and because of these chargers are charging trucks (long charging sessions --> big size logs file created per session --> ecoG storage memory filled with few files) the sessions from one week ago were already overwritten.
I had the chance anyway to analyze the logs from SCB, related to the test sessions and the events reported by you in the excel file. I attach here in the email the logs, but firstly, let me reply to your two main queries:
Only in two occasions I noticed an incorrect power allocation to the trucks. One is a known case and it will be corrected in the upcoming FW release v8.0.X, one is under investigation. In all the other cases, the power fluctuations are a normal consequence of the DynamicPowerAllocation logic of our charger, in relation to the SOC levels of the EVs.
Yes, the power delivery is of course affected by the presence of a second vehicle, according to a FIFO logic.
Let me provide you a general overview of both chargers, in terms of power allocation and power distribution. Both chargers are equipped with 15 power converters of 20kW each, so providing a total amount of 300kW power available. The converters are grouped into #4 converter groups: 60kW for the primary converter of DC1, 80kW  for the primary converter of DC2, 80kW each for the other 2 converter groups. Therefore, in case of parallel charging, the power is distributed by allocating one or more converter group to each outlet.
For a detailed analysis of the events by you reported, I created a second sheet in the excel file by you provided. There you can find an analysis of the events, and my comments, divided by green comments (no issue at all, normal behavior), yellow comments (known issues from Sicharge D that will be fixed in the upcoming FW version v8.0.X (released in CW 31 of 2025), and red comments (unknown behavior, under investigation).
At the moment, I can say that I did not see any incorrect behavior caused by these eActross trucks. The only weird behavior was on charger 170002536, where the eActross EVs was asking for low charging current, even though all the power was available.
I hope I provided you clarifications with this email and with the attached report. If you have any further question, please do not hesitate to reply to this email.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.

additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Malek,
Thank you for your feedback and your email. Today I took the time to analyze the logs and the events reported, and here is a summary of my findings:
Charger MP/R8 170002535 (tdA3ac):
​​​​​​
The charger is running with EcoG version v1.4.11 (EcoG logs have V2G pcap files).
At 2025-07-28T08:33:22 the Mercedes truck ec.94.68.00.0e.2a was connected to DC2. It failed  due to SLAC":{"link":"no PLC link". (pcap file attached:session_2-2025-07-28T08_33_32 )
At 2025-07-28T08:34:12 it was connected again to DC2, and it started charging, EV SOC 35%.
2025-07-28T08:35:48 a second truck was connected to DC1, but it failed. As you can see from the log below, no PLC link was established, and the vehicle did not even communicate the EVMAC:
2025-07-28T08:36:42.048845+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/83e1cc80f84b[737]: secc events:  {"type":"SeccSessionStop","outletId":1,"state":{"online":true,"timestamp":1753694698741,"EVCCID":"","EVMAC":"","SLAC":{"link":"no PLC link" (pcap not available, already overwritten by SECC-LE)
At 2025-07-28T08:47:51, DC2 disconnected at 45% SOC with the following error messages:
I checked with other colleagues, and apparently this is a known issue with eActross 600 trucks. It seems that sometimes, during charging session, the Pilot state drops from C to B. This could be influenced by some noise on the CP line for example, which raises the voltage of CP. This behavior has to be explained from Mercedes side. (pcap file attached:session_2-2025-07-28T08_47_00 )
At 2025-07-28T14:26:11 the Mercedes truck ec.94.68.00.0e.2a connected to DC2.
Charger went to Parameter discovery phase and then failed with error code ":39,"msg":"V2G - message timeout V2G09MSGSequence_V2GDINSession_V2GDINSession_Charging_V2GDINCableCheck". (pcap file attached: session_2-2025-07-28T14_27_00)
By checking the EcoG logs, it seems to me the EV is not sending the DINCableCheckReq. To be clarified by Mercedes why in some cases this parameter is not sent.
Charger MP/R8 170002536 (Ap1DUJ):
Unfortunately the charger is running with EcoG v1.4.5, therefore the pcap files are not available. I have installed today the v1.4.11, so to have the traces on this charger as well for the future.
I checked the sessions happened between 2025-07-28T14:36:00 and 2025-07-28T14:43:15, and they failed with the same symptoms: error code 39 for missing
DINCableCheckReq, or no PLC link.
To reply to your question in regards of the FIFO logic, please remember that each outlet has a Primary Converter Group allocated. Therefore, even if  according to the internal charger logic the first EV connected has the priority to have more power allocated, the second EV to be connected will for sure receive at least the power allocated by the primary converter group of that outlet. This is specific for the HW and FW architecture of Sicharge D.
My suggestion is, for what concerns doubts in terms of power allocation, to wait for the release of FW v8.0.X, and proceed with the analysis only afterwards. As mentioned, the FW v8.0.X will contain several improvements in terms of DPA and FIFO logic, hence it makes sense to troubleshoot this topic only after the new feature will be on the field.
Looking forward to hearing your feedback soon.

additional_info.body:
Good morning Malek,
Thank you again for your feedback and your email. Let me provide you with a detailed answer to each of your points:
We just got to know that unfortunately the release of the Sicharge D FW v8.0.X has been delayed and system tests are still ongoing. The release is now planned to happen in CW33 2025.
However, it is not totally correct to say that the FW will solve the power unbalance (such as 220kW on one outlet and 80kW on the other). As per my previous email, the architecture of the charger in terms of converter grouping is that each outlet has a CGp (Primary converter group). Therefore, if for example outlet DC1 is charging at full power and DC2 is connected, it is mandatory for the charger to de-allocate the converter group which is primary for DC2, to enable the second outlet to start charging. After this point, the logic of FIFO/FCFS is based on
EV.MAXPOWER and EV.SOC.
With the new FIFO/FCFS implementation,
a more sophisticated algorithm is introduced,
resulting in a DynamicPowerAllocation
independent
on EV.SOC levels and which provides efficient utilization of charger installed capacity by allocating/de-allocating converter groups to DC outlets based on EV power demand and is especially useful in scenarios where multiple DC outlets of charger are in charging session at same time and needs available power distributed within them
managed internally
by charger.
Further details on the new DPA implementation and new implemented features will be shared with the FW release.
To sum up, and to reply to your question, there still will be cases in which the charger will provide 220kW and 80 kW respectively to each outlet, as per correct allocation of power during parallel charging.
Yes, the sudden drop of pilot state from C-B during charging seems to be a known issue related to Mercedes and it has been observed before on other Sicharge Ds charging with eActros600.
If the communication between charger and truck cannot start, a deeper investigation with eActross should be conducted. Insights form Mercedes here are required.
In regards of the plug not being locked into the EV, please remember that the locking mechanism when using CCS2 is always inside the EV and managed by the EV. From charger side, it is only possible to visually verify that the mating frame of the plug has no damage and no dirt/dust/impurities are present.
Could you please provide me a timestamp when this issue happened, so that I can further analyze it?
Please remember that, one of the behavior of the charger which will be corrected in v8.0.X, is the inability of the charger to upscale power in certain conditions. An example of this was already presented in the excel file:
Could you please provide me with timestamps of where Mercedes claims that the charging sessions were interrupted due to temperature issues?
From a charger point of view, the temperature limit on the CCS cables is 90 degrees.
In regards of your request to have an alignment with Daimler, I am looping in this email our colleague Catalina Mora. Catalina is our Vehicle Integration expert, and she can bring insights on the analysis and underline the process and the next steps forward.
I hope I provided an answer to your questions.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!

We just got to know that unfortunately the release of the Sicharge D FW v8.0.X has been delayed and system tests are still ongoing. The release is now planned to happen in CW33 2025.
However, it is not totally correct to say that the FW will solve the power unbalance (such as 220kW on one outlet and 80kW on the other). As per my previous email, the architecture of the charger in terms of converter grouping is that each outlet has a CGp (Primary converter group). Therefore, if for example outlet DC1 is charging at full power and DC2 is connected, it is mandatory for the charger to de-allocate the converter group which is primary for DC2, to enable the second outlet to start charging. After this point, the logic of FIFO/FCFS is based on
EV.MAXPOWER and EV.SOC.
With the new FIFO/FCFS implementation,
a more sophisticated algorithm is introduced,
resulting in a DynamicPowerAllocation
independent
on EV.SOC levels and which provides efficient utilization of charger installed capacity by allocating/de-allocating converter groups to DC outlets based on EV power demand and is especially useful in scenarios where multiple DC outlets of charger are in charging session at same time and needs available power distributed within them
managed internally
by charger.
Further details on the new DPA implementation and new implemented features will be shared with the FW release.

At 2025-08-07T09:32:43 the EV is again connected. This session is successful, as SLAC communication is established.

swcpu [user:debug] [4127] [DCC]  |2025-08-07T09:32:50|DC2: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=300|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=382|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=295.9|EVSE_NowCur[A]=380|EVSE_NowVol[V]=779.6|EV_TarCur[A]=382|EV_TarVol[V]=797|EV_SOC[%]=35|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=300|Pilot=4

Availability of power to EV

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0438853-DC/Si-D/FR-[Multiple]Charging Issues on TER Transports Site CRM:00314000196
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
Please find below the report of the intervention carried out on 04/09/2025 on the TER site in Courthézon. This operation mobilized the teams of Siemens, Daimler Truck and Autorecharge.
We had two eActros 600s at our disposal (one unmodified, the other later modified by the Daimler teams) as well as a Volvo truck.
MP / R8 170002536
:
Limited power provided by the charger after temperature derating
:
After an on-site investigation, it was found that the FC20 circuit breaker on the main fan was tripped. Antoine Brua (Siemens) rearmed it and trained the operator so that this type of problem could be solved quickly without the intervention of a Siemens technician.
Sudden drop of CP line voltage during charging
:
Despite the installation of ferrites, the problem persists. The charger passes the steps of authentication, cable check, and then precharge. However, when ramping up (a few seconds after charging begins), it is interrupted due to a change in the Control Pilot signal voltage (from state C – under charge – to state B – connected). The ferrites therefore did not mitigate the disturbance on the CP line.
Tests were carried out with a KIA EV6 and a Volvo truck: the charging sessions went smoothly.
Fabien Priam (Daimler) disconnected the FDI power fuse. Following this, we were able to charge for a stable period of 10 minutes at 300 kW, which is the maximum power of the charger.
Next steps:
A meeting between Siemens and Daimler Truck is scheduled for this week in Germany Wörth. It should provide additional answers to the variations observed on the CP line.
Conclusion :
It seems that the activation of FDI on the eActros 600 causes a disturbance on the CP line when the power is ramped up, which causes the charging to stop. Tests with the Volvo Truck and KIA EV6 confirm that the charger is functional and stable.
We are waiting for the results of the meeting between Siemens and Daimler Truck in Germany to move forward in resolving this problem.
Kind regards
Catalina Mora
